newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly down but off earlier lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly down but off earlier lows.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mostly down on Monday but off earlier lows with July up on short covering ahead of Tuesday's expiration, traders said.

"You started out with the weather but after that the key factor was this July meal, (it) just won't give up," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "There are no deliveries, no selling. The July meal kept coming back, the spread kept widening and that pulled everything back up."
New crop months ended lower after rains fell across central Illinois over the weekend. More rain was forecast for Monday and Tuesday, easing concerns of moisture stress.

Forecasts called for 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rain in central Illinois through Tuesday with 60 to 80 percent coverage. Recent rains had bypassed central Illinois, leaving some fields in dire need of moisture.
Old crop months also drew support from ideas recent setbacks would attract export demand. Taiwan was expected to tender for 138,000 tonnes of soybeans this week.
Weekly export inspections data was neutral. USDA put export inspections at 6,241 million bushels.
Soybeans ended down 10-1/2 cents per bushel to up 1-1/2 with November down 10-1/2 at $5.97.
After the close of trade, USDA said 62 percent of the soybean crop was rated good to excellent, down from 66 percent the previous week.

On the day, commercials were on both sides of the market. ADM bought one million November but sold 1.5 million November. Cargill Inc bought one millio November and sold 1.5 million August. FCC sold 1.5 million November and Produce Grain bought 1.0 million November.
Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 3.5 million November and ING sold two million November, traders said.
In options trade, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 400 November $6.50 calls at 10 to 13 cents and sold 400 November $7.00 calls at six to seven cents.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 23-3/4 percent, down from 25-1/2 on Friday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 54,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 52,490 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 20,000, against Friday's 22,112.
